subject: Interactive sessions: training exclusion and subprocessor attestation
messages:
From: Lena Hoff <lena.hoff@healthsync.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Interactive sessions: training exclusion and subprocessor attestation

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the demo last week. Security has a couple of follow-ups before we sign off on the pilot:

1) We need a clear, operational commitment that interactive sessions used by end-users (chat/assistant) will not be used to improve or train any models — neither adaptive fine-tuning nor logging into training datasets. This is critical for our regulator in the EU.

2) A signed subprocessor attestation listing all subcontractors that will have access to session data (including transient KV caches or logs). We need a template we can send to procurement and legal for review.

3) A practical export pathway: we prefer SFTP export for evidence and onshore residency of exports for certain accounts. Can you confirm how Redwood would support an SFTP handoff and what subprocessors would be involved in that lane?

We are aiming to close the procurement redlines this month. If possible, please loop in the ops/infra contact who can speak to the SFTP and KMS residency guarantees.

Thanks —
Lena Hoff
Head of Security, HealthSync
[lena.hoff@healthsync.com]

[attachment: security-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Hoff <lena.hoff@healthsync.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive sessions: training exclusion and subprocessor attestation

Lena —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, details below:

- Commitment: Yes. We can contractually commit that interactive session inputs/outputs will not be used to improve models for HealthSync (no-training/no-derive for the account). We provide an operational flag at the tenant level that prevents telemetry or traces from being included in any training pipelines.

- Attestation: Im attaching our attestation template for subprocessor disclosure and signature so procurement/legal can start their review.

- SFTP export: We support an SFTP export lane for onshore evidence exports. Operationally this is delivered via a dedicated export worker and an audited transfer process; subprocessors for the export lane are CloudInfraCo (managed transfer endpoints) and SFTPPartners Ltd (managed hosting). We will provide a minimal subprocessor list for the HealthSync account.

Next steps I propose:
1) David to confirm the ops checklist and timeline for enabling the tenant-level no-training flag.
2) Kimberly to drop the attestation template and the canonical subprocessor list into the Docusign + HubSpot record.
3) Ill follow up with a short runbook for the SFTP handoff and ask for procurement timelines.

Ill attach the attestation template here.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

[attachment: subprocessor-attestation-template.pdf (PDF)]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lena Hoff <lena.hoff@healthsync.com>
Cc: ops-infra@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 12:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive sessions: training exclusion and subprocessor attestation

Lena / team —

Operational details from the infra side:

- No-training flag: We have a tenant-level configuration (accountOptOut.useForTraining = false) which prevents session token capture from being routed to any training pipelines. That flag blocks both automated telemetry ingestion and any manual inclusion into datasets. Its enforced at the routing layer and audited at request-level in our tracing system.

- Ephemeral KV & session caches: For interactive sessions we can enable ephemeral-only KV caching (TTL < 30s) and a redact-on-write path for session metadata. That ensures nothing is persisted beyond live inference for the pilot.

- SFTP export lane:
  * We will provision a dedicated export worker in the eu-central region.
  * Export worker uploads artifacts to the HealthSync SFTP endpoint using mutual-TLS and per-export signed manifests.
  * Subprocessors involved: CloudInfraCo (managed transfer nodes), SFTPPartners Ltd (SFTP host), and AuditLogStream (third-party log archival — only used for audit trail hashes, not PII).

- KMS residency: If HealthSync requires onshore KMS wrapping for export keys, we can work with your KMS provider via our key-rotation integration. We do not export unwrapped keys to subprocessors.

Timeline: We can enable the no-training flag and ephemeral mode within 3 business days after contract, and stand up the export worker in ~7 business days depending on procurement coordination for key exchange.

Action items I have taken:
- Uploaded a short Ops runbook to the Jira ticket and attached onboarding instructions for SFTP.
- Drafted the minimal subprocessor list for procurement review.

[attachment: sftp-onboarding-instructions.docx (DOCX)]

-David
David Kim
Head of Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

From: Lena Hoff <lena.hoff@healthsync.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, procurement@healthsync.com, Security Team <security@healthsync.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive sessions: training exclusion and subprocessor attestation

Thanks Sean and David — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying points from procurement/security: 

- Please convert the attestation into a signable PDF and include a one-page subprocessor table (name, role, country, purpose). Procurement will want this appended to our vendor questionnaire.

- Can you confirm whether AuditLogStream will ever be able to reconstruct full session payloads from hashes were exporting? If not, please add the explicit line: "AuditLogStream receives only hashed audit entries and cannot reconstruct user session content."

- For timeline: if the no-training flag can be enabled within 3 business days and SFTP worker within 7, wed like written confirmation (email + doc) so procurement can proceed to sign-off.

If you can send the signable attestation and subprocessor table by EOD tomorrow well circulate internally. Once procurement confirms we can lock the pilot start date.

Best,
Lena
Head of Security, HealthSync
